name: GNBG-45
description: Benchmarking studies in continuous optimization often report aggregate rankings, yet provide limited insight into why particular algorithms succeed or fail under specific landscape conditions. This paper presents a property-aware empirical assessment of ten competitive Differential Evolution (DE) variants using the Generalized Numerical Benchmark Generator (GNBG), a configurable framework that enables controlled manipulation of problem characteristics. Ten state-of-the art variants of DE are tested across three distinct datasets. The first dataset, GNBG-45, featuring 45 problem instances, each designed to isolate a single landscape property such as basin linearity, conditioning, variable interactions, symmetry or deceptiveness. The remaining datasets, GNBG-I and GNBG-II, are well established in the literature and include 24 functions each, covering unimodal, multimodal single component and multimodal multiple component problems. Together, these data sets provide a layered and comprehensive benchmarking environment. Experimental results show that ALSHADE exhibits the strongest overall robustness and consistency across diverse landscape categories and benchmark suites, while LSHADE-SPACMA exhibits the strongest scalability and robustness in multiple dimensional settings. Other variants, including IMODE, EA4eig, APSM-jSO, and TSALSHADE, demonstrate competitive behavior on selected problem classes but lower overall consistency.
